steps.name: Co-expression module detection
caveats: cor() on 6 samples has 4 df; a Pearson r of ~0.81 is nominally p<0.05, which is reached by chance often across dozens of modules

enableWGCNAThreads or allowWGCNAThreads may need to be called; blockwise functions are unnecessary at this matrix size
steps.context: This is the step that directly answers the research question. The dataset has 6 samples, which is far below the ~15-sample minimum the WGCNA authors state and the ~20+ samples conventionally used; the module structure recovered here is expected to be dominated by the single treated-vs-control contrast plus noise. steps.question: Which co-expression modules do the ~12,000 filtered liver genes form across the 6 samples, and do the module eigengenes correlate with the treated-vs-control assignment?
constraints: Use a signed network (signed or signed hybrid), not unsigned — sign-agnostic correlation is even less identifiable at this n
Set minModuleSize to at least 30 genes; do not lower it to manufacture more modules

steps.description: Using the VST matrix from T1S1, construct a signed gene-gene co-expression network with WGCNA and detect modules. steps.name: Module stability and permutation null
caveats: ARI between partitions that both contain a dominant grey module is inflated; report ARI computed both including and excluding grey-assigned genes

steps.context: This step is the honest counterweight to T1S2. Co-expression module detection at n=6 is well below any published reliability floor, and the standard failure mode is that arbitrary modules are reported as treatment-tracking on a nominal p-value that the design cannot support. Enumerating all 10 label permutations rather than sampling them is exact and cheap, and it makes the power ceiling of the design a concrete number rather than a caveat.
steps.question: How much of the module structure detected in T1S2 survives dropping a single sample, and does any module's correlation with the treated/control split exceed what the 10 possible 3-vs-3 label permutations produce by chance?
constraints: Enumerate permutations exhaustively — do not run a random permutation sampler and report a p-value smaller than 0.1
Use the same soft-threshold beta, minModuleSize and merge cut height in every LOO rerun as in T1S2; do not re-tune per rerun
If a LOO rerun fails to converge or produces a single module, report that outcome as a stability result rather than discarding the rerun
The verdict vocabulary is restricted to 'unstable' and 'stable-but-underpowered'
steps.description: Two diagnostics on the T1S2 result. (1) Leave-one-sample-out stability: rerun the full T1S2 module detection pipeline six times, each time omitting one sample (n=5), using identical parameters. For each rerun compute the adjusted Rand index and the Jaccard index of the gene-to-module partition against the full-data partition, and report per-module the fraction of its genes that stay together across the six reruns. (2) Permutation null for module-trait association: the 3-vs-3 design admits exactly C(6,3)/2 = 10 distinct label assignments, so enumerate ALL of them, recompute the module-eigengene-to-label correlation for each module under every permutation, and report each module's observed correlation's rank within its own 10-value null. State plainly that the minimum attainable permutation p-value is 0.1 and that NO module can reach conventional significance by permutation at this design. Produce a final table: module, size, observed r with treatment, permutation rank, LOO stability (mean ARI contribution and gene-retention fraction), and a verdict column of 'unstable' / 'stable-but-underpowered' — with no module allowed a 'validated' verdict.
acceptance_criteria: Six leave-one-out reruns completed with identical parameters to T1S2, each reporting its module count and partition agreement (ARI and Jaccard) with the full-data partition
Per-module gene-retention fraction across the six LOO reruns is reported
All 10 distinct 3-vs-3 label permutations are enumerated exhaustively (not sampled) and each module's observed correlation is ranked within its own null
The report states explicitly that the minimum attainable permutation p-value for this design is 0.1, so no module can be declared significant by permutation

The seed reference census confirms human hallmark (50 sets) and human GO BP (7,538 sets) gene sets are staged as symbol-keyed GMTs for Homo sapiens, and human WikiPathways is also present as a third option. constraints: Use human gene sets only — the reference store also holds mouse and rat WikiPathways and mouse hallmark sets, which must not be used on this human liver dataset
Do not run enrichment on modules that T1S3 labelled 'unstable'; list them as skipped with the reason
Every enrichment claim must carry the module's T1S3 stability verdict alongside it, so that a term is never reported without the reliability of the module it came from

If the hallmark or GO gene sets are not resolvable at run time, fall back to human WikiPathways and state the substitution; if no human gene set collection is available, report the module gene lists unannotated rather than substituting another organism

acceptance_criteria: Enrichment run against human (not mouse or rat) gene sets, with the gene symbol match rate against the GMT reported
Background universe for over-representation is the T1S1 filtered gene list, not the full annotation
Per-module enrichment tables written for every module tested, including modules with no significant terms
Preranked GSEA results on the T2S1 ranked list written with normalized enrichment scores and BH-adjusted p-values
Explicit comparison of module-derived and DE-derived enriched terms, quantifying overlap
Xenobiotic metabolism, oxidative stress and bile-acid-related hallmark set statistics reported regardless of significance

plan.title: Liver drug-treatment co-expression modules (n=3 vs 3)
plan.analytical_narrative:
The question asks for co-expression modules across samples and which modules track treatment. The data are raw Salmon gene-level counts, 12,000 genes x 6 samples (columns: 6 samples in metadata.csv, 7 columns in counts.csv = gene symbol + 6 sample columns), 3 treated vs 3 control liver samples, unpaired, single batch, Homo sapiens.

The central statistical fact that shapes this plan: with n=6 samples, every pairwise gene-gene correlation has 4 residual degrees of freedom, and after mean-centring within a two-group design the correlation structure collapses to essentially one degree of freedom of between-group contrast. Any 'module' recovered from 6 samples is dominated by the treated-vs-control split itself plus sampling noise; WGCNA's own authors state the method should not be applied below ~15 samples, and scale-free topology fitting is unstable at this n. So the plan does NOT pretend to deliver a trustworthy network. It runs the module detection the question asks for, but wraps it in explicit stability diagnostics so the output is reported with its true reliability rather than as a finding.

T1S1 builds the analysis-ready matrix: filter low-count genes, VST/log-CPM stabilise, and quantify how much of the total variance is the treatment axis vs residual — this number determines whether module detection can be anything but a treatment-split echo. T1S2 runs the actual co-expression clustering (WGCNA correlation + dynamic tree cut, with an explicit soft-threshold report and a fallback to a fixed beta when scale-free fit fails at n=6) and computes module eigengenes. T1S3 is the reliability gate: leave-one-sample-out and label-permutation resampling to measure how much module membership survives dropping a single sample, plus a null distribution for the module-trait correlation, since with 3v3 the smallest achievable permutation p-value is 0.1 (10 distinct splits) — this bound must be stated, not hidden. T2S1 runs the conventional DESeq2 treated-vs-control differential test in parallel, both as the properly-powered answer to 'what tracks treatment' and as a reference against which module-trait claims can be sanity-checked. T3S1 annotates whichever modules survive the reliability gate against human hallmark/GO gene sets so a surviving module has a biological label rather than a colour.

WGCNA minimum sample size recommendation co-expression network reliability
weighted gene co-expression network analysis sample size requirement

steps.question: What biological processes are represented by the co-expression modules from T1S2 that survived the T1S3 stability screen, and does the treated-vs-control ranked gene list from T2S1 recover the same processes?
steps.description: Two complementary annotations. (1) Over-representation analysis of each module's gene set (modules from T1S2, restricted to those not verdict-'unstable' in T1S3, with the grey module excluded and modules under 30 genes skipped) against human hallmark gene sets and human GO Biological Process sets, using the filtered gene universe from T1S1 as background rather than the whole genome. (2) Rank-based gene set enrichment (fgsea or GSEApy preranked) on the T2S1 ranked list against the same collections. Report the overlap between module-level and DE-level enriched terms — concordance is weak corroboration, discordance is a signal that the modules are noise structure. Because the liver tissue and drug-treatment context makes xenobiotic metabolism, oxidative stress and bile acid processes plausible a priori, report those specific hallmark sets' statistics explicitly whether or not they pass threshold, so that a null result on them is visible. Required reference data: human hallmark gene sets and human GO Biological Process gene sets, matched to Homo sapiens with HGNC gene symbols (the counts matrix is keyed on gene symbol, so no ID mapping should be needed; if symbols fail to match, report the match rate before proceeding).
steps.context: Modules and DE lists are only interpretable once they carry biological labels. The seed reference census confirms human hallmark (50 sets) and human GO BP (7,538 sets) gene sets are staged as symbol-keyed GMTs for Homo sapiens, and human WikiPathways is also present as a third option. All are HGNC symbol space, matching the gene symbol row keys of counts.csv.
acceptance_criteria: Enrichment run against human (not mouse or rat) gene sets, with the gene symbol match rate against the GMT reported
Background universe for over-representation is the T1S1 filtered gene list, not the full annotation
Per-module enrichment tables written for every module tested, including modules with no significant terms
Preranked GSEA results on the T2S1 ranked list written with normalized enrichment scores and BH-adjusted p-values
Explicit comparison of module-derived and DE-derived enriched terms, quantifying overlap
Xenobiotic metabolism, oxidative stress and bile-acid-related hallmark set statistics reported regardless of significance
constraints: Use human gene sets only — the reference store also holds mouse and rat WikiPathways and mouse hallmark sets, which must not be used on this human liver dataset
Do not run enrichment on modules that T1S3 labelled 'unstable'; list them as skipped with the reason
Every enrichment claim must carry the module's T1S3 stability verdict alongside it, so that a term is never reported without the reliability of the module it came from

If the hallmark or GO gene sets are not resolvable at run time, fall back to human WikiPathways and state the substitution; if no human gene set collection is available, report the module gene lists unannotated rather than substituting another organism
caveats: GO BP sets are hierarchically nested, so significant terms arrive in correlated blocks — collapse redundant parent/child terms before reporting a count
Over-representation on a module that is itself a treatment-split artifact will still return terms; enriched terms do not rescue an unstable module
A module of a few hundred genes drawn from a 12,000-gene liver matrix will trend toward generic liver and metabolic terms by composition alone
